title: Base case of the well-ordered union projective resolution argument
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, M an R-module, E a linearly ordered well-ordered set, and F : E → Submodule R M a monotone family with every element of M in some F e. Let U e be the supremum of stages F i with i < e, pulled back into F e. If every quotient F e / U e has a projective resolution of length at most zero [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], then M has one of length at most zero.

proof.text: (Case $n=0$: the quotients are projective and the projections split.) For $n=0$ a projective resolution of length $\le0$ of $Q_e=M_e/M_{<e}$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module] is an exact sequence $0\to P_0\to Q_e\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], i.e. an isomorphism $P_0\cong Q_e$ with $P_0$ projective; hence $Q_e$ is projective [lem-weil-pbc-projective-direct-summand] (2). The sequence $0\to M_{<e}\to M_e\xrightarrow{q_e}Q_e\to0$ ($q_e$ the quotient map, surjective with kernel $M_{<e}$) is short exact with projective quotient, so there is an $R$-linear section $s_e:Q_e\to M_e$ with $q_e\circ s_e=\mathrm{id}_{Q_e}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ses-projective-quotient-splits]. Choose one $s_e$ for every $e\in E$ (axiom of choice), regard it as a map to $M$, and let $\psi:\bigoplus_{e\in E}Q_e\to M$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] be the $R$-linear map $\psi((x_e)_e)=\sum_es_e(x_e)$ (a finite sum). In Lean use categorical projectivity from the length-zero augmentation being an isomorphism, and categorical splitting of the quotient epimorphism. This avoids a Small R hypothesis.

proof.text: ($\psi$ is surjective, by transfinite induction.) Suppose not. Since $M=\bigcup_eM_e$, the set of $e\in E$ with $M_e\not\subseteq\operatorname{Im}\psi$ is nonempty; as $E$ is well-ordered it has a least element $e$, so $M_{e'}\subseteq\operatorname{Im}\psi$ for every $e'<e$, hence $M_{<e}\subseteq\operatorname{Im}\psi$. Take $y\in M_e\setminus\operatorname{Im}\psi$ and $x_e=q_e(y)\in Q_e$. Then $q_e(y-s_e(x_e))=x_e-x_e=0$, so $y-s_e(x_e)\in M_{<e}\subseteq\operatorname{Im}\psi$, and $s_e(x_e)=\psi(\iota_e(x_e))\in\operatorname{Im}\psi$ ($\iota_e$ the canonical inclusion). So $y\in\operatorname{Im}\psi$, a contradiction. Thus $\psi$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: (Conclusion for $n=0$.) $\bigoplus_eQ_e$ is projective as a direct sum of the projective modules $Q_e$ [lem-weil-pbc-projective-direct-sum-family] (Stacks 065Q, which the source cites), so $M\cong\bigoplus_eQ_e$ is projective [lem-weil-pbc-projective-direct-summand] (2), and $0\to M\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}M\to0$ is a projective resolution of length $\le0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. This is $C(0)$. For independent index and module universes, shrink the external direct sum along its linear equivalence with M, and prove categorical projectivity of the shrunk sum by lifting each quotient component and summing on finite supports.
